_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 3.2. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Which is the correct definition of robbery?
options: Stealing and, immediately before or at the time of doing so and in order to do so, using force on any person or putting/seeking to put any person in fear of being then and there subjected to force

questions.scenario: LEE honestly believes BEN owes him £50. He punches BEN and takes £50 from his wallet. Is this robbery?
options: Yes, because the money was not LEE's
No – there is no theft because LEE was not dishonest (s. 2(1)(a)), so no robbery
Only if he used a weapon
explanations: Correct: R v Robinson (1977) – assault offences may apply.
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.2 · No theft, no robbery – Robinson

questions.scenario: Two youths push and jostle a man so he loses his balance, and one takes his wallet. Is there enough force for robbery?
options: Yes – force is an ordinary word and minimal force can suffice
Only if a weapon is used
explanations: Correct: R v Dawson and James (1976).

questions.scenario: A woman holds her handbag tightly. A man wrenches it from her grip and runs. Which is correct?
options: Only theft, as force was on the bag
Robbery – force on the bag transmitted to her can be force on the person

questions.scenario: During a shop theft, the suspect pushes a security guard (not the owner) out of the way to take the goods. Can this be robbery?
options: No, force must be on the owner
Only if the guard is injured
Yes – force can be used on any person
Only if the guard owns the goods

questions.scenario: A man tells a woman: 'Give me your phone tomorrow or I'll beat you up next week.' She hands it over the next day. Is this robbery?
options: No – the fear must be of being then and there subjected to force
Only if he had a weapon
explanations: Fear of future force is not enough.

questions.scenario: HALE and an accomplice take jewellery from a bedroom, then tie up the householder before leaving the house. Is the force 'at the time of' stealing?
options: No, the theft was complete before the force
Only if they used a knife
Yes – appropriation can be a continuing act (R v Hale (1978))

questions.scenario: A shoplifter is challenged outside the shop after the theft is complete and pushes the guard away only to escape. Which is most accurate?
options: Usually not robbery – force used only to escape after the theft is complete is not 'in order to steal' (consider facts)
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.2 · Purpose – in order to steal

questions.scenario: Does the victim actually have to be put in fear for robbery by threats?
options: No – it is enough that the defendant sought to put a person in fear
Only if a weapon is shown
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.2 · Seeking to put in fear

questions.scenario: How is robbery tried?
What is the maximum sentence for robbery?
A man threatens a cashier with a knife to make her open the till, but police arrive before he takes anything. Which offence?
options: Assault with intent to rob (s. 8(2)) or attempted robbery
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.2 · s. 8(2) – assault with intent to rob

questions.scenario: A man punches a victim out of anger. Ten minutes later, seeing the victim's wallet on the floor, he picks it up and leaves. Is this robbery?
options: Yes, because force preceded the theft
No – the force was not used in order to steal

questions.scenario: Snatching a mobile phone loosely held in someone's hand with no force on the person is…
options: possibly only theft – it depends on whether force was used on the person

questions.scenario: A robber says to a victim 'hand over your bag now or I'll stab you', but the victim is not scared at all. Which is correct?
options: No robbery because she wasn't afraid
Robbery if he steals – he sought to put her in fear of force then and there
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 3.2 · Seeking to put in fear

questions.scenario: Which element is NOT part of robbery?
options: Timing and purpose of the force

questions.scenario: A robber uses force on a victim's friend standing next to her so he can take the victim's bag. Can this be robbery?
options: Yes – force on any person in order to steal
No, force must be on the victim
Only if the friend is injured
Only if the friend owns the bag

questions.scenario: A man threatens a shopkeeper: 'If you don't give me the cash now, I'll smash your face in.' He gets the cash. Which is correct?
options: Robbery – fear of force then and there in order to steal

questions.scenario: To prove robbery, which must the prosecution prove about the theft?
options: All the elements of theft (dishonesty, appropriation, property, belonging to another, ITPD)

questions.scenario: A suspect pretends to have a gun in his pocket and demands a phone from a teenager, who hands it over. Is this robbery?
options: No, because there was no gun
Only if the gun was real
Yes – he sought to put the victim in fear of being then and there subjected to force

questions.scenario: A man uses force on a woman to take her car keys, intending only to drive the car around and return it. Is this robbery of the car?
options: Not robbery of the car if there is no intention to permanently deprive (no theft); consider other offences
explanations: Correct (consider robbery of the keys if ITPD exists for them, TWOC, assault).

questions.scenario: Which is a correct statement of the timing rule?
options: Force must be used immediately before or at the time of stealing
Force can be used at any time after the theft
Force must be used a day before

questions.scenario: A man pulls a woman's handbag; she holds on and is dragged a short distance before letting go. Is this robbery?
options: Yes – force was used on her in order to steal

questions.scenario: Which is NOT required for robbery?
options: Use of force or fear of force
That the force is in order to steal

questions.scenario: An offender robs a petrol station with a knife. Which other offence might also be considered depending on facts?
options: Possession of an offensive weapon / bladed article

questions.scenario: Assault with intent to rob under s. 8(2) is…
A victim gives his wallet to a robber who threatened immediate violence. Has the robber 'appropriated' the wallet even though the victim handed it over?
options: Yes – consent obtained by threats does not prevent appropriation
Only if the robber grabbed it
Only if the wallet contained cash
explanations: Not genuine consent; and appropriation can occur with consent.

questions.scenario: A robber knocks a man unconscious and then takes his watch. Which is correct?
options: Not robbery because the victim was unconscious when the watch was taken
Robbery – force used immediately before stealing and in order to steal

questions.scenario: Which statement about the threat of force is correct?
options: Only threats to the owner count
Threats can be to put any person in fear

questions.scenario: A man says to a shop assistant: 'Give me the money or I'll burn your house down tonight.' Which is most accurate?
options: Not robbery (no fear of force then and there); consider blackmail
